selection: step-out from bonsai1/L5/N7124- (10x queue, model pilot: sonnet)

neighbours.label: stem pieces of split negated adjectives after in-/un-/il- (inflexible, intolerable, ungrateful, ilimitado)
fire: The regime was known for its inflexible and intolerant rules.
She felt ungrateful for complaining about the free ticket.
Servers offer unlimited storage and indiscriminate access to files.
El plan incluye un número ilimitado de entradas gratuitas.
His intolerable rudeness made the dinner unbearable for everyone.
The judge called the claim indisputable and the evidence uncontroversial.
It was an unprecedented and inexcusable failure of oversight.
Their immodest boasting and impatient replies annoyed the committee.
quiet: The regime was known for its strict and harsh rules.
She felt thankful for receiving the free ticket.
Servers offer large storage and careful access to files.
El plan incluye un número reducido de entradas gratuitas.
His constant rudeness made the dinner tiresome for everyone.
The judge called the claim valid and the evidence clear.
It was a serious and costly failure of oversight.
Their modest boasting and patient replies pleased the committee.

notes: Model pilot (sonnet arm; the same pole is tested independently by the other arm, pairing disclosed): this pole feeds the held pole bonsai1/L5/N7124- (zeroing this neuron removes 0.60 of the anchor's peak), from a batched edge measurement with 8 same-layer placebos. Label and all 16 sentences written by the Sonnet 5.5 labeller from a packet (card + all-pole band samples + the edge hint) and one probe round of 8 sentences (none reused). An Opus gate checked rule-level items only and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Probes: the stem pieces after the negating prefix scored 0.6-0.84 in English and Spanish, and the positive forms (flexible, tolerable, grateful, elevado) were ~0, so the prefix matters. Near misses swap in non-negated synonyms; fire items vary the stems because the piece, not one word, carries it.
